topic: What Is Engineering Mechanics? Forces and Force Systems
title: What Is a Force? Explained Simply | Engineering Mechanics Ep 1
description:
Kiran pushes an old auto rickshaw. Salim chacha pulls it with a rope. They both pull hard, yet the auto swerves toward the wall. Why? In this animated lesson we meet Salim Auto Works, a small repair workshop in Peenya, Bengaluru, where a team will turn one old diesel auto into an electric auto called Bijli, one engineering mechanics idea at a time.

You will see R. C. Hibbeler's textbook definition of mechanics, the two branches (statics and dynamics), what a force really is (size, direction, point of application and line of action), and why one newton is about the weight of a 100 g apple. Then we replay the push like engineers: Kiran's 200 N and Salim's 300 N at 30 degrees added tip to tail into a 484 N resultant that drifts toward the wall, against a straight pull of 500 N. We sort forces into collinear, concurrent, parallel and general force systems, see them at work in a railway, a crane, a bridge and a signboard, and look at the limits honestly, including the 1940 Tacoma Narrows Bridge.

This is Episode 1 of our Engineering Mechanics series for B.E. and B.Tech Mechanical students and GATE ME aspirants. Example figures are for illustration.
